text.p: Impoverished Yemen is facing a population explosion and needs family planning, new jobs and improved public services to cope with the rising number of citizens, a Yemeni official said on Wednesday.

"Yemen's population is 16.75 million now. And with the current annual growth rate of 3.7 percent, it could reach 31.5 million in the year 2013," said Mohammad Ali al-Haj, secretary general of the National Population Council.
"We have a population explosion on our hands that needs to be addressed with family planning, job creation schemes, adequate health care and other services," he told a news conference.
Al-Haj said statistics showed six babies were born in Yemen every five minutes.
Yemen, one of the Arab world's poorest states, is suffering from 100 percent annual inflation and unemployment ranging from 30 to 50 percent.
The government is currently implementing the second phase of economic reforms agreed with the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund.
